title: Superregular solitonic solutions of the defocusing nonlocal nonlinear Schrodinger equation and their novel perspectives
abstract: Previous studies have indicated that the local defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE) is modulationally stable. Therefore, superregular solitonic solutions characterizing the nonlinear evolution of modulational instability under weak localized perturbations do not exist. In this work, we study the nonlinear stage of the modulation instability of a condensate in the framework of the defocusing nonlocal NLSE. By using the dressing method and Joukowski transformation, we systematically derive the general $N$-solitonic solution of the defocusing nonlocal NLSE, and the explicit expressions for one-solitonic, two-solitonic and superregular two-solitonic solutions are provided. Then dynamics of these solutions is also examined. We find that these solutions show a much wider variety than those in the local NLSE, such as the one solitonic solution composed of two interacting wave components and the two-solitonic solution containing four wave components. Finally, the accuracy and noise robustness of the analytical solutions are confirmed by numerical simulations. Such results advance the theory of superregular solitonic solutions in nonlocal systems and offer new physical understanding of wave propagation in nonlocal nonlinear media.
summary: This paper develops the theory of superregular solitonic solutions for the defocusing nonlocal nonlinear Schrödinger equation using the dressing method. It derives explicit analytical forms for multi-soliton solutions and confirms their stability and robustness via numerical simulations. The findings advance the understanding of wave propagation in nonlocal nonlinear media.
main_problem: The study investigates the existence and properties of superregular solitonic solutions for the defocusing nonlocal nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE) during the nonlinear stage of modulation instability.
main_result: The paper successfully derives general N-solitonic solutions and confirms the existence of superregular solutions for the nonlocal defocusing NLSE, which contrasts with previous findings for the local case.
method: The authors employ advanced mathematical techniques, specifically the dressing method combined with the Joukowski transformation, to systematically derive the exact analytical solutions.
model_or_system: The model is the defocusing nonlocal NLSE, analyzed in its reverse-time form. The system describes nonlinear wave propagation in nonlocal media, relevant to fields like nonlinear optics.
key_observables: N-solitonic solutions, one-solitonic solution (composed of two interacting wave components), two-solitonic solution (containing four wave components), and the stability/robustness against noise.
important_parameters: Defocusing regime ($\sigma = -1$), the number of solitons ($N$), and the initial perturbation strength.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the dressing method and assumes specific asymptotic constraints on the dressing function $\chi(\lambda)$ to derive the general solution structure.

Figures illustrate the profiles of superregular two-solitonic solutions, showing the difference between elastic coalescence ($z_1=z_2$) and separation ($z_1

paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical context (MI in nonlocal NLSE) to deriving the general N-solitonic solution using the dressing method. It then provides explicit forms for one- and two-solitonic solutions, concluding with numerical verification of the analytical results.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous analytical solutions for complex wave phenomena (superregular solitons) in nonlocal media, which is highly relevant for theoretical quantum optics and nonlinear wave dynamics.
